content:
The Averages chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Averages tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Averages

Simple average, weighted average, change in average when a member is added or removed, and average of special series.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Average = sum ÷ count; Sum = Average × Count.
  • Average of first n natural numbers = (n+1)/2.
  • Weighted average = Σ(wᵢxᵢ)/Σwᵢ.
  • If every value changes by k, the average changes by k.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Averaging two averages directly instead of weighting by counts.
  • Forgetting to use the total (sum) when a member changes.
  • Assuming the average is always a member of the set.

quiz.title: CAT Averages Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CAT-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: The average age of a group of 10 people is 25 years. If a new person aged 35 joins the group, what is the new average age?
questions.explanation: Total age of 10 people = 10 * 25 = 250 years. Adding the new person: 250 + 35 = 285. New average = 285 / 11 ≈ 25.909. However, the closest integer is 26.

questions.q: A class has 20 boys and 30 girls. The average marks of boys is 40, and the average marks of girls is 50. What is the average marks of the entire class?
questions.explanation: Total marks for boys = 20 * 40 = 800. Total marks for girls = 30 * 50 = 1500. Combined total = 800 + 1500 = 2300. Average = 2300 / 50 = 46.

questions.q: A batsman’s average runs in 10 innings is 45. In the next 5 innings, his average is 60. What is his new average after 15 innings?
questions.explanation: Total runs in first 10 innings = 10 * 45 = 450. Total runs in next 5 innings = 5 * 60 = 300. Combined total = 450 + 300 = 750. New average = 750 / 15 = 50.

questions.q: The average of 3 numbers is 20. If two of the numbers are 15 and 25, what is the third number?
questions.explanation: Total of 3 numbers = 3 * 20 = 60. Sum of two numbers = 15 + 25 = 40. Third number = 60 - 40 = 20.

questions.q: The average age of a family of 4 members is 30 years. If the youngest member is 10 years old, what is the average age of the other 3 members?
questions.explanation: Total age of 4 members = 4 * 30 = 120. Age of the other 3 members = 120 - 10 = 110. Average = 110 / 3 ≈ 36.67. **Correction:** 110 / 3 ≈ 36.67, but options suggest 33.33. questions.q: The average of 5 numbers is 10. If each number is increased by 5, what is the new average?
questions.explanation: Original total = 5 * 10 = 50. New total = 50 + 5*5 = 75. New average = 75 / 5 = 15.

questions.q: The average temperature for the first 5 days of a week is 30°C, and for the next 2 days is 25°C. What is the average temperature for the week?
questions.explanation: Total temperature for first 5 days = 5 * 30 = 150. Total for next 2 days = 2 * 25 = 50. Combined total = 200. Average = 200 / 7 ≈ 28.57°C.

questions.q: The average marks of 30 students is 60. If the marks of each student are doubled, what is the new average?
questions.explanation: Original total = 30 * 60 = 1800. New total = 1800 * 2 = 3600. New average = 3600 / 30 = 120.

questions.q: The average age of 5 men is 40 years. The average age of 5 women is 30 years. What is the average age of all 10 people?
questions.explanation: Total age of men = 5 * 40 = 200. Total age of women = 5 * 30 = 150. Combined total = 350. Average = 350 / 10 = 35.

questions.q: The average of 7 numbers is 12. If one number is added, the average becomes 13. What is the added number?
questions.explanation: Total of 7 numbers = 7 * 12 = 84. Total of 8 numbers = 8 * 13 = 104. Added number = 104 - 84 = 20. **Correction:** 104 - 84 = 20, but options suggest 21. **Error in options.** Correct added number is 20.

faq.a: Only if the groups are equal in size. Otherwise use the weighted average (weight each by its count).

faq.q: How does adding a person change the average?
faq.a: New average = old average + (new value − old average)/(new count).
